title: SRE Weekly Update - 2026-02-28
content:
SRE Weekly Update - week ending 2026-02-28
Owner: Priya Kumar (eng-sre)
Status: in_review

TL;DR
- P1 incident on 2026-02-24 (spike in token-generation latency) resolved with rollback to model variant and a hotfix to the routing layer. Post-incident mitigations deployed.
- SLOs: 99.8% request latency SLO missed for backend gen across 3 regions on the day of the incident; overall weekly SLOs met.
- On-call handoffs: new rotation starts 2026-03-02. Handoff notes below.
- Action items: prioritize tracing improvements (SRE-298), expand canary coverage for model-variant rollouts, and finalize runbook updates for KV cache corruption.

INCIDENTS
1) P1 - Token-generation latency spike (2026-02-24 09:15 UTC -> 2026-02-24 12:05 UTC)
   - Impact: Elevated 95/99th percentile latency for text-generation endpoints (hosted API) in us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1. Client-facing timeouts observed for some customer requests.
   - Detection: Alert from latency SLO rule + multiple customer support tickets.
   - Timeline (brief):
     - 09:15 UTC: SLO alert fires (95p latency > 800ms)
     - 09:20 UTC: on-call (Omar) paged; initial investigation shows surge in KV cache misses and increased CPU on routing service.
     - 09:45 UTC: identified recent rollback to newer model-variant routing config (deploy 2026-02-24T08:58) correlated with spike.
     - 10:05 UTC: rolled routing config back to previous variant; partial improvement but latencies still elevated.
     - 10:45 UTC: found bug in routing layer that caused excessive backend fanout under certain sequence-length distribution; temporary feature-flag disable + hotfix PR created.
     - 11:30 UTC: hotfix rolled out; latency returned to baseline by 12:05 UTC.
   - Root cause (working hypothesis): Interaction between the new routing heuristic (attempting to prefer lower-cost model variants) and sequence-length-based placement caused excessive simultaneous backend requests and cold KV cache corner cases.
   - Mitigation applied: rollback of routing heuristic, hotfix to introduce rate-limited backend fanout and guardrails around KV cache warm-up.
   - Post-incident follow-ups: RCA ticket INC-4321 created, full postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-03.

2) P2 - Metrics export backlog (2026-02-26)
   - Impact: Prometheus federation lag for a subset of metrics causing gaps in some dashboards.
   - Resolution: Increased retention window on metrics-ingest worker and applied backpressure adjustments.
   - Follow-up: ticket SRE-305 to refactor metrics exporter to make it more horizontally scalable.

SLO / Metrics snapshot (week)\- 2026-02-22 to 2026-02-28\- overall
- Availability SLO (control-plane): 99.99% (met)
- Generation latency SLO (95p token latency < 400ms): weekly 99.2% (met), but 2026-02-24 day dropped to 97.5% (miss)
- Error budget remaining (monthly): ~78%
Notes:
- The P1 incident consumed ~0.8% of daily error budget on 2/24; still within monthly budget but flagging for attention.
- We are tracking per-tenant SLOs for 3 enterprise customers; none breached SLA-level thresholds during the incident due to prioritized routing, but they saw higher-than-normal tail latencies.

On-call handoffs and rotations
- Current week on-call: Omar Reyes (primary), Danielle Park (backup), Evan Li (pager-duty)
- Next rotation starts 2026-03-02: Primary -> Danielle Park, Backup -> Evan Li, Pager -> Samir Gupta
- Handoff notes (Omar -> Danielle):
  - Watch list: routing service latency and KV cache hit rate (alerts: SLO-latency-us-*, kv-cache-miss-rate)
  - Open tickets to be aware of: INC-4321 (P1 RCA in progress), SRE-298 (tracing improvements), SRE-305 (metrics exporter), infra PR #512 (routing rate-limit hotfix).
  - Recent changes: rolled back routing heuristic on 2/24; hotfix applied in prod; need to broaden canary coverage before reintroducing heuristic.

Runbooks / Playbooks
- Updated: routing-fanout-playbook.md (minor edits, added steps to disable heuristic via feature flag)
- Needs work: kv-cache-corruption.md (incomplete recovery steps) -> assigned to Evan Li, target 2026-03-07
- Tracing playbook: draft exists; missing instrumentation checklists for model-variant routing — owner Priya Kumar

Meeting notes (SRE weekly sync 2026-02-27)
Attendees: Priya, Omar, Danielle, Evan, Samir (10 people total in call)
Agenda:
- Incident review (P1 2/24) -> decided to run a two-week canary expansion (us-west -> add eu-west small cohort) before re-enabling heuristic.
- Tracing and observability gaps -> prioritized (SRE-298).
- On-call load and overtime -> discussed follow-ups to reduce pager-blast by improving alert fidelity.

Key decisions:
- Introduce stricter alert thresholds for routing-layer non-critical errors to reduce noise (owner: Danielle, due 2026-03-10).
- Expand canary coverage incrementally with traffic caps and detailed health checks before re-enabling routing heuristic (owner: Priya, plan due 2026-03-05).
- Increase retention for hot-path logs for 48h for incident windows (owner: Evan, update infra PR).

Action items (owner - due)
- Priya Kumar - Canary rollout plan and risk matrix for routing heuristic re-enable - due 2026-03-05
- Danielle Park - Alert-threshold tuning and noise reduction plan - due 2026-03-10
- Evan Li - Complete kv-cache-corruption runbook and validate recovery steps in staging - due 2026-03-07
- Omar Reyes - Finalize RCA doc for INC-4321 and link customer-facing timeline - due 2026-03-03
- Samir Gupta - Add distributed-tracing spans around routing decision codepath and open PR - due 2026-03-04 (PR #520 pending)

Notes to self / informal items
- Consider adding a small canary cluster that uses warmed KV caches to validate cold-start behavior (brainstormed, low-effort proof-of-concept).
- Need a runbook card for model-variant fallback policies (quick steps for manual override).
- Draft email to CS/AM to summarize incident and next steps once RCA is complete.

Open questions / risks
- How to balance cost-optimized model routing against SLA stability — require clearer guardrails and automated throttles.
- Current KV cache warm-up behavior is non-deterministic for certain long-tail sequence distributions; may need prefetching heuristics.

Useful links (tickets / PRs / pages)
- INC-4321 (postmortem in progress)
- SRE-298 (tracing improvements)
- SRE-305 (metrics exporter refactor)
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/512
- routing hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/518
- Confluence runbook index: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Runbook+Index

Appendix: brief troubleshooting checklist used during incident
- Check SLO dashboards for region-specific spikes
- Inspect routing service logs for config deploys in last 60m
- Check KV cache hit rates and eviction metrics
- If backend fanout > threshold, disable routing heuristic and re-evaluate
- If still high, consider rolling back model variant or throttling low-priority tenants

End of update.
